reconcile.definitions:
The two statements measure different units with different probabilities. The model generation is not what separates them.

PUBLISHED 70 (and 555)
- Source chain: scripts/textmodel_batch.py (the night run) -> utdata/textmodel_batch/sammanstallning.json (textmodel-18) -> utdata/modellartikel/runstenar.py -> runstenar.json['batch']['runsten'] -> build_modellartikel_data.py D['batch'] -> build_modellartikel.py.
- Stones: every Viking-age inscription in tm._records()['V'] that has at least one run of lost runes the panel can fill. Stones with fewer than 4 readable runes are dropped: 58 runestones, including Öl 57 and Ån Fv1908;298A. Only Rundata object containing 'runsten' is counted, so fragments and lost stones are in; grave slabs, rock faces, slate pieces and loose objects are out.
- Unit: one row per gap as the app's panel builds it (src/textmodel.py _read). Lost runes inside one divider-delimited group are merged with rl.merge_runs. A merged run with more than MAX_GAP = 4 lost runes is not filled at all (it goes in 'open_gaps').
- Editor status: a panel gap is matched to the first overlapping gap from scripts/runlm_gaps.gaps_of in the same carved group. scripts/luckprov.status_of then sets the status: '[' in Rundata's token means återställt; token None or '...' means ej återställt; anything else is oklart, and unmatched gaps are 'utanför provet'.
- Probability: the panel's CALIBRATED percentage for the gap's top word, words[0]['p']. This is the joint list calibration tm.calibrate_words (gap_list in data/runlm_calibration.json), fitted at the level of the documented gaps.
- Model: the fold model that has not seen the stone (tm.bundle(tm.fold_of(sig)), crc32 mod 5). It is held out per stone, with no loo.
- Result: restored = 555 runestone gaps, 267 of them calibrated >= 0.95. Open = 70 gaps on 57 runestones, 0 of them >= 0.95.

CURRENT FORSKNINGSLUCKOR 848 / 175 / 27
- Source chain: scripts/runlm_gaps.py (run via the tm19 pipeline with own_d, name_cands 40, lam_class 0.2, tolerance 0.02, context_cands, by_word, near 0.1/10 km, max_gaps 2000) -> utdata/runlm_forfining/tm19/klass3_alla.json -> scripts/textmodel_candidates.py -> data/textmodel_candidates.json (copied to /Volumes/2TB/cache/perf/textgaps.json) -> GET /api/research/gaps/textmodel (api/routers/research.py line 92) -> web/src/app/(app)/luckor/page.tsx.
- Stones: Rundata Viking-age inscriptions with transliteration and normalization from Swedish provinces (G.SW). ALL object types are included: 175 open = 112 runestone gaps, 18 on other stones and 45 on loose objects.
- Unit: every single run of 1-4 '-' inside a carved word, with words split on Rundata's spaces and dividers. The word must keep at least 2 preserved runes. The oklart status is excluded. In total 848 = 673 restored + 175 open. Runs close together are filled jointly by merge_runs, but the merged span has NO 4-rune cap. For example, U 525 au--s--þ-- has three 2-rune runs in one span of 6 lost runes, and U Fv1946;258 -i-a-----i-iti has a span of 8. The inventory fills only its sampled gaps, not every lost rune on the stone, so the context differs from the panel's. U 765 a-s shows this: hans at 0.995 in the list, 0.29 raw and 0.36 calibrated in the panel.
- Probability: r['p'] = words.get(word), the RAW marginal word probability from rl.restore_all. No calibration is applied anywhere in runlm_gaps.py or textmodel_candidates.py; runstenar.py calibrates this same field itself with C.features(x['p'], ...). The page and METHODS.md section 14 nonetheless call it 'kalibrerad sannolikhet' (page.tsx about line 1156; METHODS.md about line 1406). The 'Byggd' date is the file mtime, 2026-10-20.
- Model: also held out per stone, but the folds are i % 5 over the sorted stone list, not crc32. The model is the textmodel-19 settings.
- Result: 27 candidates with raw >= 0.80 and a known word, on 21 inscriptions (18 rows on runestones, 9 on other stones and loose objects). Rows with raw >= 0.95 and a known word: 12 rows on 10 inscriptions (14 if two <unk> rows are counted). reconcile.explanation:
The difference has five causes, largest first.

1) RAW against CALIBRATED probability. This is the main cause. The published sentence uses the panel's calibrated percentage. The list shows the model's raw word probability while calling it calibrated. The calibration pulls high raw values down a lot, most of all for names and rare words, and the open gaps are full of those. Raw -> calibrated under textmodel-19:
- Sm 47 þikra 0.996 -> 0.902
- Sö 280 þæiRa 0.974 -> 0.651
- Ög 115 fyrir 0.969 -> 0.627
- Sö 245 mag 0.939 -> 0.631
- U 784 ok 0.962 -> 0.899
- U 1180 risti 0.955 -> 0.866
- U 522 heðingunnr 0.924 -> 0.487
- U 466 viseti 0.796 -> 0.441 (textmodel-18: 0.995 -> 0.931)
- U NOR2000;34B skeþ 0.904 -> 0.571
- U 441 arnilli 0.905 -> 0.414
Even under textmodel-18, the published 70 held 5 gaps with raw >= 0.95 and 16 with raw >= 0.80. On the restored side the raw count would have been 339 of 555, not 267.

2) Different population. The published figure counts runestones only. The list includes Sö 280 and Sö 23 (other stones), U Fv1946;258 (berghäll), Ån Fv1908;298A (skifferbit), the U NOR1994;26A amulet, and the U NOR2000;34B and U Fv1992;161B bones. Of the 12 rows at 95 % or more, 2 are not on runestones.

3) Different unit. The panel will not fill a merged run of more than 4 lost runes, and the inventory has no such cap. So U 525 hiortstaðum (6 lost runes), U NOR1994;26A fængit and fly, Öl ATA4377/56A ok (7) and U Fv1946;258 viseti (8) are not filled by the panel at all. Öl 57 ræisa and Ån Fv1908;298A guð have fewer than 4 readable runes, so the panel cannot read them. The inventory also splits on Rundata's word spaces, so one panel gap can be several rows. U 525 contributes 3 rows to the 12.

4) Different reading context. The inventory fills only its sampled gaps; the panel fills every fillable gap together. This is why U 765 hans is 0.995 in the list but 0.29 raw in the panel.

5) Model version. This is minor, and it pushes the other way. The textmodel-18 inventory (utdata/runlm_forfining/klass3_alla.json) already had 14 open runestone gaps at raw >= 0.95 (15 across all objects) in the same 848/175 frame. textmodel-19 has 10 (12). The new model did not create the 95 % gaps; the old inventory had them too.

Under the published definition with textmodel-19: 0 of the 70 open runestone gaps reach calibrated >= 0.95. The highest is Sm 47 þikra at 0.902. Four reach 0.80 or more: Sm 47 þikra 0.902, U 784 ok 0.899, U 1180 risti 0.866 and Öl ATA4701/43 ok 0.819. Under textmodel-18 there were three. The set of 70 is identical, because the gap structure comes from the text and not from the model. I did NOT recompute the restored side ('267 of 555') for textmodel-19. It would need the full batch of 1,383 stones; I started it and stopped it because the machine was heavily loaded. That half of the sentence therefore remains a textmodel-18 figure.

reconcile.recommendation:
1) Do not set the list's '99.8 %' against the article's 'aldrig 95 %'. Readers would see a contradiction where there is only a scale difference. In the new article, give every candidate the panel's CALIBRATED percentage (textmodel-19: Sm 47 þikra 90 %, U 784 ok 90 %, U 1180 risti 87 %, Sö 280 þæiRa 65 %, U 522 heðingunnr 49 %, U 466 viseti 44 %, U 441 arnilli 41 %, U NOR2000;34B skeþ 57 %). Where only a raw figure exists, because the panel does not fill the gap (U 525 hiortstaðum, NOR1994;26A fængit, Öl 57, Ån Fv1908;298A), give that raw figure and say plainly that it is the model's own figure before calibration. Count runestones and other objects separately, as the object-types rule requires. Suggested sentence (sv):
"I artikeln Runorna som fattas skrev vi att modellen aldrig säger sig vara minst 95 procent säker i de luckor som utgivarna lämnat öppna. Det gäller fortfarande med den nya versionen: av de 70 öppna luckorna på runstenar når ingen dit, och högst kommer þikra på Sm 47 med 90 procent. Procenten i listan nedan är något annat. De visar hur mycket bättre ordet passar runorna och sammanhanget än alla andra ord modellen känner till, före den kalibrering som prövats mot utgivarnas facit. Sådana siffror blir lätt höga – i tolv luckor över 95 procent – men de betyder inte att stenen säkert säger så."

2) The published article needs no correction of fact. Under its own definition (calibrated, runestones, panel gaps) the sentence holds with textmodel-19 too: 0 of 70. Its restored half (267 of 555) is still a textmodel-18 figure; I did not recompute it. If a clarification is wanted when the new article goes out, patch it in via Firestore only (never --update), straight after "…påstår sig modellen alltså aldrig veta.":
"(Siffran gäller appens kalibrerade procent för luckorna som panelen fyller på runstenar. Listan under Forskningsluckor visar modellens okalibrerade sannolikhet för ordet och tar med alla slags föremål; där når några öppna luckor över 95 procent.)"
English: "(The figure refers to the app's calibrated percentages for the gaps the panel fills on runestones. The list under Research gaps shows the model's uncalibrated word probability and includes all kinds of objects; there some open gaps exceed 95 per cent.)"

3) Separate from the articles, for Viktor to decide: the Forskningsluckor page (web/src/app/(app)/luckor/page.tsx about line 1156) and METHODS.md section 14 (about line 1406) call the list's p 'kalibrerad sannolikhet', but it is the raw restore_all marginal. Either fix the label to 'modellens egen (okalibrerade) sannolikhet', or build the list from calibrated panel values. The page text 'runstenarnas texter' should also say that 9 of the 27 rows are on other stones or loose objects. I changed nothing in the repo.

stones.place: Klista, Vårfrukyrka sn, Åsunda hd, Enköping (Uppland); the stone is in two parts: one raised near Klista, the other in Enköpings museum

gaps.literature: SRI 8 (Upplands runinskrifter 3), U 765, pp. 327–329 (Pl. 88, 89). Edition reading: '. . k . . . . . . . - n : h. . . s l - . . . - : a - s : -' (letter-spaced pdftotext output, alignment uncertain). Comment: 'R. 11 torde vara a. Av r. 12 återstår hst och möjligen spår av en bst t. v. om hst. 13 s förefaller att vara säkert, likaså det följande sk.' Conclusion: 'Inskriften är tyvärr alltför skadad för att tillåta ett tolkningsförslag.' SRI proposes no restoration for r. 12 and no interpretation of the word. Rundata 3.1 and Runor 2020 both transliterate '-...k...-...-n : h...sl-...- : a-s : -...' with normalisation '... ... ... ...'. Rundata 'other' field: 'Stille (1999b:53) läser -...k...-...-n : h... : slþ...- : a-s : -...'. Stille thus also reads a-s and, as Rundata reports it, gives no restoration. Rundata attributes the stone to Tidkume (A) after Stille 1999b. The Swedish runic bibliography (riksarkivet.x-ref.se) lists only Oehrl 2011 (iconography) and Lucas 2020 (inventory) for U 765. I have not read either.

Stille 1999b (Runstenar och runristare i det vikingatida Fjädrundaland, Uppsala diss.): NOT reachable. The URN urn:nbn:se:uu:diva-51 resolves to uu.diva-portal.org diva2:165999, but the TLS handshake fails from this machine (curl: LibreSSL SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL) and WebFetch failed with 'Socket is closed'. gaps.traces: SRI 8 p. 328 describes the surface as heavily weathered with large flaked areas, and says the blasting shot in the back 'har skadat ristningsytan svårt'. For the gap rune (r. 12) SRI records 'hst och möjligen spår av en bst t. v. om hst'. The flanking runes are 11 a ('torde vara a') and 13 s ('förefaller att vara säkert'). SRI p. 328 also says runes 7–14, the gap included, are on the fragment kept in Enköpings museum, not on the part raised at Klista.
gaps.dividers_matter: The proposal does not depend on word division. SRI calls the divider after r. 10 'relativt säkert' and the one after r. 13 secure. Rundata and Stille (via Rundata) also give ': a-s :'. The three-rune word is therefore bounded by carved dividers. 'hans' here means the h-less spelling 'ans' (a + n + s). That spelling is attested nearby, e.g. U 785 Tillinge 'halbi : ant : ans' (SRI 8 p. 368).
gaps.assessment: This is a formula word inside a divider-bounded slot of three runes, two of which the edition considers read. The model weighs 'hans' (as ans) at 99.5 % against ars (0.2 %) and alls/als (0.1 %). The surrounding text is uninterpretable according to SRI, so the choice rests mainly on the a?s frame and the frequency of the word, not on context. The model's context reading 'sal hans' presupposes reading the preceding 'sl-...-' (Stille: 'slþ...-') as sal, which no edition does. Confirmation or refutation needs inspection of r. 12 on the Enköping museum fragment (SRI Pl. 88–89, or a new photo or scan), to see whether the staff and possible left branch fit n rather than r or l. Low content value even if right.

Confirming it would need Stille 1999b:57f, the ATA Dnr 365/61 report, and a photo of the fragment carrying -uk, to see whether a divider or a word start precedes the lost rune. As things stand, this is a weak candidate to publish.

The whole carving is weathered: rune 2 is uncertain, rune 7 is "osäkert", and rune 10 and the last rune are only faint vertical strokes.
gaps.dividers_matter: Yes, decisively. There are no dividers. The text stands in three separate rows on the two short sides of a slab (rows 1–9 on one side, 10–13 on the other; Rundata marks the row breaks with '¶'). The model's reading 'pai þikra gæiRrøð' runs straight across those breaks: þikra joins the end of row 1 (þ + the filled rune) to the start of row 2 (kra), and gæiRrøð joins the last rune of row 2 to the row on the opposite short side. The proposal exists only if the rows are read as one continuous text, which Kinander says they are not.
gaps.assessment: Very weak, despite p = 0.998. The 'word' þikra is not an attested Old Norse word. It occurs in Rundata only as the uninterpreted sequence <þikra> on Ög 60, so the model is matching one unexplained hapax. The reading crosses row breaks and the two short sides of the slab. The edition says the runes give no coherent text. Rundata and Kinander/Gardell question whether the slab is Viking Age at all: it may be modern or a 12th-century grave slab. The only thing the model has right is that a single staff fits the trace. This should be removed from the candidate list. If anything, it is an example of the segmentation weakness, and it calls for a filter that excludes medieval or possibly modern objects and readings that cross row breaks.

gaps.traces: SRI 2 p. 113: f is certain. Of the second rune only 'vänstra hälften' of R is visible, so Rundata marks it uncertain, (R). After that come 26 cm up to the next colon, with no runes identified (Rundata: two lost runes). Brate says other indistinct runes 'skönjas' but could not be determined. The whole stone is 'mycket förvittrad'.
gaps.dividers_matter: Yes, but in the proposal's favour. The group is bounded by colons on both sides (': f(R)-- :'), so the word division is given by the carver and the gap must be the end of a one-word group. The concern is the spelling, not the segmentation. The model's fill 'ri' gives fRri, a spelling of fyrir that occurs in Rundata only on N 235 (medieval Norway). The R itself is only half visible.
gaps.assessment: This is a formula word inside dividers, so the model is predicting the kind of function word that any runologist would consider. The edition gives no reading and nothing that supports or contradicts fyrir. The proposal rests on a half-visible R, and the resulting spelling fRri is very rare in the corpus. Nordenskjöld's older reading has the preposition eftiR in the text; Brate rejected that reading as a whole, but it is a competing preposition. The proposal could be confirmed or refuted on a raking-light photo or scan of the 26 cm after the R: fyrir needs two runes, r and i. Until then it is a plausible guess at a function word, not a finding.

gaps.literature:
SRI 1 (Ölands runinskrifter, Brate after Söderberg), p. 125, describing Rhezelius' 1634 drawing: "vid den andra ormens stjärt med åtta runor, ... af hvilka de första äro tre stafvar, följda af ×, 4—5 ra, 6—7 oläsliga, 8 a." Rune 5 carries footnote 1, "utskr." followed by a variant rune form, so Rhezelius' fair copy shows rune 5 differently. Brate also says the drawn runes "utgör slutet af en inskrift" (same page). Neither he nor anyone else proposes a word.
Källström, M. 2020, "En återuppstånden runsten från Källa ödekyrka på Öland (Öl 57)", Futhark 9–10 (2018–2019): 179–191, DOI 10.33063/diva-401071. On p. 180 he writes that the fragment kept "åtta runor i rundjurets svans, varav de flesta tycks ha varit mer eller mindre oläsliga, men där åtminstone × ra och en avslutande a-runa kunde urskiljas. Detta är vad som är känt av inskriften på Öl 57 och det är naturligtvis omöjligt att tolka." Using Wallman's drawings he joins Rhezelius' fragment to the Ahlqvist/Wallman fragment and the 1960 finds. On p. 189 he gives the whole text as "…skar… [lit ×] ṛitạ [× stain × þị…--- + ra--a]", normalised "… lēt rētta stæin þe[nna] …". The final ra--a is left uninterpreted.
Runor 2020 (RAÄ) adopts that reading and normalisation, and the Rundata logbook 2014–2020 (Owe) has the same entry for Öl 57. Rundata 3.1, which the model reads, still has only "[...--- + rn--a]" with normalisation "... ...". Ljung 2016, vol. 2, cat. no. 140 (p. 94) repeats "[…--- + rn--a]", normalisation "...", with no comment.

SRI 1 Ölands runinskrifter, häfte 2, p. 125 (raa.se PDF sri_oland_b01_h02.pdf; page image checked)
Källström 2020, Futhark 9–10: 179–191 (fetched via Wayback copy of the DiVA PDF diva2:1385971; DiVA itself refused TLS from this machine)

Not read: Rhezelius F c 5 original (seen only as reproduced in Källström fig. 1); Boström 1969 (Sveriges kyrkor 128); Bruce Nilsson 1973 nos. 171–173 (UMI dissertation, not online); ATA Dnr 4022/71
gaps.traces: The gap is known only from Rhezelius' 1634 drawing of a fragment now lost. SRI 1 p. 125 calls runes 6–7 "oläsliga" (illegible). Källström p. 180 says most of the eight runes seem "mer eller mindre oläsliga" and that only × ra and a final a could be made out. No source describes the strokes in the two lost places, and nothing can be checked on the stone. The editions also disagree with Rundata 3.1 on the second carved rune: SRI, Källström and Runor read 'a' (ra--a), while Rundata 3.1 has 'n' (rn--a). The model's input is the Rundata 'rn--a', so its tolerance layer had to treat that n as an a.
gaps.dividers_matter: Partly. A divider (+ in Rundata and Runor, × in Källström) stands before r, and the final a is the last rune of the inscription, so the five-rune span is bounded on both sides. Inside the span no dividers are recorded. The proposal assumes ra--a is one word; nothing in the drawing shows whether it is one word or two.
gaps.assessment: Weak, despite the 96.9 %. The letter frame r-a-?-?-a matches ræisa, but four things count against relying on it. The only witness is a 17th-century drawing in which the two runes are illegible. The model's input carries the Rundata 3.1 'n', which the editions do not read. Källström's reconstruction (Futhark 9–10, pp. 186 and 189) shows that the same inscription already has the raising formula 'lit × rita × stain × þi…' before this point, and Brate and Källström agree that these runes end the inscription, where a second raising verb would be unexpected. The model scored the gap without that context, because Rundata 3.1 lacks it. Nobody can confirm or refute it on the stone, since that part is lost. A sensible next step is to rerun the model on the Runor 2020/Källström text (…lit × rita × stain × þi…--- + ra--a) and to re-examine Rhezelius' original drawing (KB F c 5) and the Bautil copy. Until then, treat it as a letter-pattern match, not a restoration.

gaps.traces: No source describes what is visible in the three lost places. The KMB photo description (Bengt A. Lundberg 1991) says "Reliefhugget fragment funnet 1951. Texten är mycket nött och tolkning saknas för närvarande." Ljung 2016 records three fragments (67×33×6, 40×33×6, 16×15×6 cm), relief, "Rest av zoomorf ornamentik". The two readings differ inside and around the gap. Rundata has u - - - k i r k r a. Owe (1998) has a bind-rune s^u, then - - e k - r k r a: he reads an e in the third lost place, where the model puts r, and gives no i where Rundata has one.
gaps.dividers_matter: Yes, decisively. No divider is recorded anywhere in 'u---kirkra', in Rundata or in Owe's reading. The model's fill k-a-r makes 'uk' a word (ok) and starts a new word with the remaining runes. Rundata's space before u is an editorial word division, and Owe reads that u as part of a bind-rune s^u, so u may not even begin a word. On spelling: SRI 1, Inledning p. 13 (Söderberg) states for the Öland inscriptions "konjunktionen »och» skrifves alltid auk". In Rundata's Öland transliterations the form auk occurs 44 times and uk 3 times (not checked whether all three are ok).
gaps.assessment: Weak. The high word probability rests entirely on the model's own segmentation of a sequence without dividers. The word itself is the commonest function word and would add nothing to the content. The model's whole reading of the passage ('<unk> ok arngærðr gærva <unk> i') has only 65 % probability. The only other independent reading (Owe 1998) disagrees with the fill in the third lost place, and his bind-rune s^u makes a word-initial u uncertain. 'uk' is also a minority spelling of ok on Öland. Examining the stone or the CC BY 2.5 KMB photos for the lost places (k? a? r/e?) and for any divider before u would confirm or refute it, and so would reading Owe's report ATA Dnr 411-4568-1998.

stones.place: Strängnäs domkyrka, Strängnäs (Södermanland); red sandstone grave slab (gravhäll), formerly in the cathedral floor

gaps.literature: Rundata 3.1 normalization: "Ulfrik ok þa ... fæðga ok <-aua>"; Runor 2020 the same ("ok þa … fæðga"). The gap is open in every edition checked. SRI 3 (Brate & Wessén, Södermanlands runinskrifter, 1924–36), p. 245, translation: "efter Ulvrik och . . ., fader och son". SRI p. 246 treats the gap as one of the inscription's names: "Tyvärr höra inskriftens namn till dess mest skadade eller svårlästa partier" … "De båda återstående namnen kunna ej fastställas." (the other name is 69–72 kaua). The grammar comment is on p. 246: "Språkligt intressanta äro de båda uttrycken þau Undrlaug møðgini och (ack.) þa . . . fæðga". SRI makes no restoration of þ--a and does not suggest a pronoun. SRI p. 246 also says Ulfrik occurs "på en uppländsk runsten (Lingsberg, Vallentuna sn)", which is U 241. In Rundata, U 241 is one of the only two parallels for the bigram þæiRa fæðga ("Guð hialpi þæiRa fæðga salu"). The other is Sö 347 "hialpi and þæiRa fæðrga".

gaps.traces: SRI p. 245: "52 a—57 þ äro mindre tydliga men dock säkra. Efter 57 þ ytterligare 3 (högst 4) runor i ordet, varav den sista är a (tydligt). Därframför nedre delen av en stav, som lutar svagt åt vänster; snarast u, möjligen r." The stone surface is worn by trampling, since the slab lay in the church floor: "numera delvis utplånad genom trampning" (p. 244). The older readings all have the gap: B 700 "þ—a"; Dybeck, Hermelin and Brate "þ—a"/"þ--a" (p. 245).
gaps.dividers_matter: Word division is secure. The carved text has a divider on each side of the word: "auk · þa · þ--a · faþka". The gap size is not secure. SRI allows 3, at most 4, runes after þ including the final a, so the lost part may be 2 or 3 runes. The model assumes exactly 2, filled as iR.
gaps.assessment: This is a weak proposal. It conflicts with grammar, with the editor's trace and with the editor's reading. The model's 97 % comes from the bigram þæiRa fæðga, which occurs only in prayers where a governing noun requires the genitive (Sö 347 and U 241, and U 241 also names an Ulfrik). On Sö 280 the phrase stands after æftiR, where SRI explicitly marks þa . . . fæðga as accusative and reads the gap as a lost name. SRI's trace before the final a is "snarast u, möjligen r" (ᚱ), not the ᛦ that the model's fill iR needs. SRI also allows a 3-rune gap. Close inspection of the slab or of the public-domain detail photos could support the proposal, if it showed a stave fitting ᛦ and a 2-rune space. A u trace, or room for three runes, would refute it. Either way, the case problem would remain.

(1) The Inskrift line "auk • þa • þ - - a • faþka" is on p. 245, with the translation "efter Ulvrik och . . ., fader och son". (2) The trace note is also on p. 245: "Efter 57 þ ytterligare 3 (högst 4) runor i ordet, varav den sista är a (tydligt). Därframför nedre delen av en stav, som lutar svagt åt vänster; snarast u, möjligen r." The same page gives the older readings: "B 700: ... 57—60 þ—a", Dybeck/Hermelin "þ—a", Brate "þ--a". (3) "Tyvärr höra inskriftens namn till dess mest skadade eller svårlästa partier" is at the foot of p. 245, not p. 246 as the finding says. (4) "De båda återstående namnen kunna ej fastställas" and "Språkligt intressanta äro de båda uttrycken þau Undrlaug møðgini och (ack.) þa . . . fæðga" are on p. 246. (5) "numera delvis utplånad genom trampning" is on p. 244. SRI gives no restoration and suggests no pronoun; it treats the gap only as an unidentified name. To try to refute this, I checked several more sources. None restores the gap. Rundata 3.1 (local): normalization "Ulfrik ok þa ... fæðga", translation_en "in memory of Ulfríkr and they ... father and son". RAÄ Runor 2020: "ok þa … fæðga", with no notes. rundata.info/inscription/so-280 has the same normalization; its English translation reads "Ulfríkr and ..., this father and son", and it lists the references Ljung 45, Liljegren p. 117, Bautil p. 196. Liljegren, Run-urkunder 1833, L 958 (local PDF, page 112) reads "Ulfrik. auk pa. p..a. fapita..". The parallels claim also holds: in the local Rundata, þæiRa fæðga occurs only in U 241 (Lingsberg, which names Ulfrik) and Sö 347 (þæiRa fæðrga). I could not check Nordiskt runnamnslexikon (Peterson 2007). The isof.se paths I tried returned 404, and the old sprakochfolkminnen.se link from the World Tree Project page was not tested. So a later name proposal recorded in NRL cannot be excluded. Note: þ-u-r-a, Þóra (the accusative of Þóri), would match SRI's u/r trace and the accusative. No source I saw makes that proposal; this is only a remark from me.

gaps.traces: No edition describes traces in the gap. Rundata and Runor mark one lost rune after ma. SRI p. 215 says only that the ring (slingan) is damaged ("Utom slingan, som är skadad"). The fragment measures 0.62 × 0.86 m. SRI's illustration is Pl. 191, from Brate's 1900 drawing or photo in ATA.
gaps.dividers_matter: Word division is secure: "ul : ma- : san" has dividers on both sides. The proposal depends on the gap being exactly one rune, and the following san read as sinn. Spelled "man", mann would also fill one rune (the model gives it 0.02).
gaps.assessment: This is a strong proposal, but it is not new. The Runor 2020 editors already normalise ma[g] sinn, so the model reproduces an existing editorial restoration. It counts as independent agreement, not a discovery. The formula 'æftiR X, mag sinn' is well attested (about 20 Rundata texts). The main alternative with the same spelling length is mann ("man"), which the model rates 2 %. gaps.literature: SRI 3 (Brate & Wessén), p. 16, interprets the end as a prayer with "ande" (soul) in this passage, but it aligns the runes differently from the model. In SRI's words (OCR text): "dess slut tyckes hava varit välgångsönskan för hans själ: Gud hjälpe ande och själ! Ordet »Gud» är tydligt i Fa. 35—37, B. 27—29 kuþ; av »hjälpe» finns blott Fa. 38 a, B. 30—32 ai i, av »ande» Fa. 39 t, B. 33—34 it". SRI's resulting text ends "Gud hjälpe ande och själ!" and is introduced with the caveat "Av dessa osäkra och inbördes skiljaktiga läsningar kan blott en osäker tydning bitvis erhållas" and "Om förestående slutsatser äro riktiga". SRI thus takes the a as a remnant of hialpi and only the t as a remnant of and, with an unknown number of runes lost between them. Wikell & Johnsson, Fornvännen 107 (2012), pp. 16–23, p. 20, report a different wording: "Med förbehåll meddelar han i Södermanlands runinskrifter följande (osäkra) inskrift: »… Gud hjälpe hans själ!»". That paraphrase drops "ande", and they make no reading of their own: "Tolkningen av dessa överlämnas till runologerna". Rundata 3.1 and Runor 2020 have no normalization (all '…'). Rundata's note says "Bureus läsning enligt Fa. 10. 2 s. 83 används".

Wikell & Johnsson, Fornvännen 107 (2012):16–23. The fornvannen.se and pub.raa.se links failed from this machine (TLS/timeout), so it was read from the arild-hauge.com mirror, saved as /Volumes/2TB/cache/luckor-del3/pdf/so23/fv2012_016.pdf
gaps.traces: There are no physical traces. This part of the inscription is lost. Rundata brackets the whole passage as known only from older drawings ("[· ai...oþi · kuþa-t auk... o...]"). Wikell & Johnsson (Fv 2012, p. 20) could read only "…nta…" on the surviving 30 × 60 cm patch and state: "Resten av hällen är ohjälpligt bortvittrad." The sequence kuþa-t comes from Bureus's 17th-century drawing (Fa. 10. 2 s. 83), already "Fördärvad af eld" (SRI p. 16). Bautil (B 784) gives the same stretch differently: "kuþa i-...itak · sio..." (Rundata note). SRI counts B. 30–32 "ai i" and B. 33–34 "it" here, so B 784 suggests more than one sign between a and t.
gaps.dividers_matter: Yes, the proposal depends on division. kuþa-t has no divider inside it. The model splits it as kuþ | a-t and fills one rune (n) to make guð and, with no verb (hialpi) between. SRI divides it as kuþ | a[…] | […]t, with hialpi in between. The one-rune size of the gap rests on reading Bureus's '-' as exactly one rune. Bautil's version (i-...it) does not support that.
gaps.assessment: The word itself is weakly supported. Literature and model agree that "ande" belongs in this prayer, which is a formula that is easy to guess. They disagree on how the carved runes are divided. The model's guð and without hialpi is not the usual Christian prayer formula, and SRI's alignment needs more lost runes than the one the model assumes. The source is a pair of mutually inconsistent 17th-century drawings of a fire-damaged surface that no longer exists. The proposal cannot be checked against traces, and it adds nothing beyond SRI's own uncertain interpretation. Only the original Bureus drawing, viewed as an image, could show how much space the lacuna has.
